label: input token k at original positions 2-6
explanation: Fires only when the input token is k during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at positions t=2..6. It is silent on k at t=0,1 and at t>=7, on the delimiter, and on the copy phase (essentially zero mass there, even when the model outputs k). Magnitude is highest at t=3-5 (about 90% of mass), weaker at t=2 and t=6. Activation is larger on the first occurrence of k in a sequence; a repeated k usually fires more weakly. Remaining false positives are mostly k at t=2 or t=6 where the feature stays off.

issues: The claim that a repeated k fires more weakly is wrong when checked on k only. On dev, for k at t=2-6 with n_seen([k])>0, precision is 0.945 and the case holds 12.4% of activations but 14.1% of the activation mass. For first-occurrence k, precision is 0.884 with 87.6% of activations and 85.9% of the mass. So repeated k fires slightly more often and slightly more strongly than first k. The explanation should drop or reverse this sentence. It does not affect the label or predicate.

The false positives are almost entirely at the edges. Precision is 1.0 at t=3, 1.0 at t=4 and 0.9998 at t=5, but only 0.66 at t=2 and 0.82 at t=6. The t=2 rate is flat across L (0.65-0.67 for L=3..9), so length is not the cause.

Whether k fires at t=2 depends strongly on which tokens came before it, with no simple pattern. By previous token: a 0.93, q 1.0, 0 0.93, versus m 0.12, d 0.24, x 0.24. By the token two back: d and k 1.0, versus 0 0.10 and b 0.32. Digit versus letter, vowel, in_count and n_digits splits do not separate it cleanly. These cases carry little mass (t=2 is 4.6% of the mass, t=6 is 4.9%) and no compact rule captures them, so I treat this as noise at the activation threshold rather than a counterexample class.

Copy-phase silence holds almost exactly. There are 10 dev activations outside the original phase (26 in test, about 0% of the mass), all tiny (0.03-0.12 of max) and mostly when k is fed back as an input at the first copy steps. One test miss is a weak activation (0.03) on a k at t=7. The 'about 0% outside the predicate' claim checks out.

The other claims check out. Dev precision is 0.891, recall 0.9997 and mass recall 0.99996. Test precision is 0.890, recall 0.9996 and F1 0.941. The t=3-5 positions hold about 90% of the mass (0.334+0.354+0.217). The feature never fires on k at t=0 or t=1, never on the <DEL> step, and never on any other input token. Dropping t=2 lowers test F1 to 0.883, so including t=2-6 is justified.
